title: Federal AI procurement mandates frontier-model cyber attestations by Q2 2027
body: The Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security executive order is written to be light-touch on its face: it explicitly bars any reading that authorizes mandatory governmental licensing, preclearance, or permitting, and the frontier-model early-access track is framed as strictly voluntary. The teeth arrive through a different channel. The order directs Treasury, NSA, and CISA to build a benchmarking process, designate covered frontier models by reference to their offensive and defensive cyber capability, and stand up an AI Cybersecurity Clearinghouse that coordinates vulnerability scanning and patch distribution across federal and critical-infrastructure systems the government itself buys. That combination - a government-run designation list plus federal buying power flowing through the clearinghouse - is the classic path by which a nominally voluntary framework becomes a de facto seller requirement. The prediction is that by Q2 2027 the executive branch converts the framework into a procurement condition: a Federal Acquisition Regulation amendment, an agency acquisition rule, or standardized solicitation clause will require vendors of covered frontier models selling into federal use to attest that they participate in the cyber-capability benchmarking and the early-access disclosure process, with at least three covered-frontier vendors publishing such attestations or winning awards bound to the clause. This mirrors how prior cyber executive orders (secure-software self-attestation under the CISA repository) turned guidance into a contracting gate without new statute, and it is the executive-branch counterpart to the separate congressional catastrophic-risk disclosure debate rather than a restatement of it.

reasoning.because: Ropes & Gray + Freshfields flag the EO bars licensing yet creates procurement pull on frontier labs
reasoning.given: Treasury/NSA/CISA designate covered frontier models and run a clearinghouse agencies buy into
reasoning.so_that: An acquisition rule or solicitation clause requires covered-model vendors to attest to the voluntary cyber framework
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; >=3 covered-frontier vendors publish federal cyber attestations
reasoning.plain_language: After the order said it will not license AI, the government starts requiring sellers to prove their cyber safety to win contracts.

summary: The EO bars mandatory AI licensing but leans on federal procurement and the new AI Cybersecurity Clearinghouse. Expect an acquisition clause requiring covered-frontier-model vendors to attest to the voluntary cyber framework, with at least three publishing attestations by Q2 2027.
